chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Abu Jamilah, from al-Ridha عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who bequeathed a sword to another man, and it was in a sheath and had adornment upon it. The heirs said to him, "Only the blade belongs to you, and the sword does not belong to you." So he said, "No; rather, the sword with what is in it belongs to him."

He said: I said to him, a man bequeathed a صندوق to another man, and there was wealth in it. The heirs said, "Only the صندوق belongs to you, and the wealth does not belong to you." So he said, "The صندوق with what is in it belongs to him."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: made a bequest or testamentary gift
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةُ: the heirs disputing the extent of the bequest
key_terms.بِسَيْفٍ: a sword specified in the bequest
key_terms.بِصُنْدُوقٍ: a chest or box named in the bequest
key_terms.حِلْيَةٌ: adornment or decorative fitting attached to the sword
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or money found inside the box

ai.seo_question: If someone bequeaths a sword or a box, does the bequest include what is with it or inside it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bequests: when a person bequeaths an item, what is ordinarily included with or inside that item is also included in the bequest. The Imam عليه السلام rules that a sword includes its sheath and adornment, and a صندوق includes the wealth inside it. The narration is significant in jurisprudence for clarifying how testamentary language is understood in practical legal disputes.
